papers.summary: We introduce an approach that creates animatable hu-man avatars from monocular videos using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Existing methods based on neural radi-ance fields (NeRFs) achieve high-quality novel-viewlnovel-pose image synthesis but often require days of training, and are extremely slow at inference time. Recently, the com-munity has explored fast grid structures for efficient training of clothed avatars. Albeit being extremely fast at training, these methods can barely achieve an interactive ren-de ring frame rate with around 15 FPS. In this paper, we use 3D Gaussian Splatting and learn a non-rigid deformation network to reconstruct animatable clothed human avatars that can be trained within 30 minutes and rendered at real-time frame rates (50+ FPS). Given the explicit nature of our representation, we further introduce as-isometric-as-possible regularizations on both the Gaussian mean vectors and the covariance matrices, enhancing the generalization of our model on highly articulated unseen poses. Experi-mental results show that our method achieves comparable and even better performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches on animatable avatar creation from a monoc-ular input, while being 400x and 250x faster in training and inference, respectively. Please see our project page at https://neuralbodies.github.ioI3DGS-Avatar.

papers.title: SplattingAvatar: Realistic Real-Time Human Avatars With Mesh-Embedded Gaussian Splatting
papers.authors: Zhijing Shao, Zhaolong Wang, Zhuang Li, Duotun Wang et al.
papers.what: [Conference] We present SplattingAvatar, a hybrid 3D representation of photorealistic human avatars with Gaussian Splatting em-bedded on a triangle mesh, which renders over 300 FPS on a modern GPU and 30 FPS on a mobile device. We disentangle the motion and appearance of a virtual human with
papers.summary: We present SplattingAvatar, a hybrid 3D representation of photorealistic human avatars with Gaussian Splatting em-bedded on a triangle mesh, which renders over 300 FPS on a modern GPU and 30 FPS on a mobile device. We disentangle the motion and appearance of a virtual human with explicit mesh geometry and implicit appearance modeling with Gaus-sian Splatting. The Gaussians are defined by barycentric coordinates and displacement on a triangle mesh as Phong surfaces. We extend lifted optimization to simultaneously op-timize the parameters of the Gaussians while walking on the triangle mesh. SplattingAvatar is a hybrid representation of virtual humans where the mesh represents low-frequency motion and surface deformation, while the Gaussians take over the high-frequency geometry and detailed appearance. Un-like existing deformation methods that rely on an MLP-based linear blend skinning (LBS) field for motion, we control the rotation and translation of the Gaussians directly by mesh, which empowers its compatibility with various animation techniques, e.g., skeletal animation, blend shapes, and mesh editing. Trainable from monocular videos for both full-body and head avatars, SplattingAvatar shows state-of-the-art ren-dering quality across multiple datasets. Code and data are available at https://github.com/initialneil/SplattingAvatar.

papers.title: Unrolled gradients in disguise: bridging interpolation-based and Jacobian regularization for stable neural dynamics
papers.authors: Maya Janvier, Etienne Meunier
papers.what: [Conference] Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergenc
papers.summary: Hybrid models and neural differential equations (NDEs) are becoming increasingly important for modelling physical systems; however, they often encounter stability and accuracy issues during long-term integration. Training on unrolled trajectories is known to limit these divergences but quickly becomes too computationally expensive due to the need to compute gradients over an iterative process, making this method impractical for large-scale physical systems (e.g. weather and climate forecasting). Two popular paradigms for improving the stability of learned dynamics are to train on interpolated or noisy samples or to regularize the Jacobian of the learned representation. In this work, we demonstrate that these paradigms can be understood under a common lens and that they both correspond to an approximation of the gradients obtained in an unrolled learning strategy. Building on this understanding, we derive a principled and complete approach to regularize training and demonstrate its impact on the stability of learned dynamical systems.

papers.title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
papers.authors: Kara D. Lamb
papers.what: [Conference] Earth system models (ESMs) rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence. However, translating advances in physical understanding into stable, validated parameterizations and integrating them into ESMs often tak
papers.summary: Earth system models (ESMs) rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence. However, translating advances in physical understanding into stable, validated parameterizations and integrating them into ESMs often takes years. Agentic AI could accelerate this process and enable more systematic exploration of design choices. Using warm-rain collision-coalescence as a test case, we evaluate agents' ability to synthesize scientific literature, reimplement published bulk parameterizations, and propose new functional forms as differentiable JAX code. We compare conventional parameterizations, data-driven emulators, and agent-generated closures against high-fidelity superdroplet simulations, repeating unattended experiments across ten language models. With expert guidance or iterative feedback, agents produced executable, differentiable, mass-conserving code, although unattended performance depended strongly on the scheme and language model. Iterative feedback lowered median rollout error for eight of ten models. Retuned physical schemes matched or outperformed many learned parameterizations at substantially lower computational cost, but two of 100 unattended agent-generated closures achieved slightly lower rain-mass error than the most accurate retuned scheme on held-out simulations.

papers.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
papers.authors: Yuxuan Jiang, Chenglin Liu, John Rose, Mason Miller et al.
papers.what: [Conference] LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on small-scale settings such as self-contained Python modules, leaving distributed systems, an essential class of product
papers.summary: LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on small-scale settings such as self-contained Python modules, leaving distributed systems, an essential class of production software, under-examined. We introduce DistDebug-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' ability to diagnose complex-system failures at the code level. It curates 120 high-quality real-world bugs from 11 widely used distributed systems, spanning 5 programming languages and 10 failure patterns. Through an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs and agents, we identify substantial gaps between current agents and real-world debugging tasks. A recurring gap is tunnel vision due to a lack of explicit reasoning structure and nondeterminism from inconsistent tool-use scope. The benchmark and evaluator are available at https://github.com/OrderLab/distdebug-bench, with agent traces and a leaderboard at https://distdebug.com.

papers.title: Algorithmic Intervention Decreases Polarization in Content Moderation
papers.authors: Anna Bertani, Saeedeh Mohammadi, Taha Yasseri
papers.what: [Explore] Crowd-based moderation relies on people's collective judgments to combat misinformation, but raters bring their own ideological biases to the task, shaping how they moderate each other's contributions. We ask whether an algorithmic redesign can counteract this bias, using X's Com
papers.summary: Crowd-based moderation relies on people's collective judgments to combat misinformation, but raters bring their own ideological biases to the task, shaping how they moderate each other's contributions. We ask whether an algorithmic redesign can counteract this bias, using X's Community Notes, where contributors write context for potentially misleading posts and rate each other's notes. Community Notes replaced simple majority voting with an algorithm that instead rewards agreement across people with different ideological viewpoints. Comparing 8,805 notes and 4,367 contributors before and after this change, we find that ideological polarization decreased in the algorithm's estimates of contributor and note positions. Although negative interactions increased, contributors became less structurally aligned, indicating that negative interactions were less organized along partisan lines. These findings show that algorithmic incentives can reshape both the social structure and behavioral dynamics of crowds, extending beyond their intended effects on content moderation.

papers.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
papers.authors: Mohamed Nomeir, Sennur Ulukus
papers.what: [Explore] We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled stat
papers.summary: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.

papers.title: When Covariates Mask Pre-Trends
papers.authors: Parush Arora
papers.what: [Explore] Honest difference-in-differences methods judge how far parallel trends may fail after treatment by how far it failed before treatment, as shown by placebo estimates. When the design adjusts for covariates, the placebo estimates are adjusted too. We show that this benchmark is val
papers.summary: Honest difference-in-differences methods judge how far parallel trends may fail after treatment by how far it failed before treatment, as shown by placebo estimates. When the design adjusts for covariates, the placebo estimates are adjusted too. We show that this benchmark is valid only if the covariates are measured before the earliest placebo window. A covariate measured later already reflects shocks to the outcome during the placebo period, so adjusting for it hides part of the pre-trend. The placebos then look flatter than the true trend and the resulting confidence sets are too narrow. When the covariate is also observed at an early date, the distortion can be estimated and tested. Of 90 recent published studies that adjust for time-varying covariates, 77 measure at least one covariate too late.

papers.title: Mediating Human-Swarm Interactions Through a Robot Helper: A Shepherding-Inspired Approach
papers.authors: Arihant Yadav, Sophie Jörg, Eakta Jain
papers.what: [Explore] This work investigates human-swarm interaction (HSI) for steering large collectives through an intermediary robot helper. While prior robot-swarm control and HSI techniques commonly assume swarm members are addressable, these assumptions often fail for ``ungovernable'' swarms suc
papers.summary: This work investigates human-swarm interaction (HSI) for steering large collectives through an intermediary robot helper. While prior robot-swarm control and HSI techniques commonly assume swarm members are addressable, these assumptions often fail for ``ungovernable'' swarms such as wildlife flocks and schools of fish. Motivated by pastoral shepherding, we compare low-level teleoperation to a higher-autonomy motion-primitives interface in a virtual reality (VR) shepherding task under varied swarm cohesion dynamics. Results indicate that motion primitives that operate on collective shape (e.g., boundary-based control) improve task performance and reduce perceived workload.

papers.title: Specification LASSO and a Flexible Characteristics-Based Asset Pricing Model
papers.authors: Chaohua Dong, Shuyi Ge, Shaoran Li, Wen Su
papers.what: [Explore] This paper studies a partially linear semiparametric additive model that allows for interactions among variables in high-dimensional settings. We propose the Specification LASSO (S-LASSO), a two-step method that integrates LASSO and Adaptive Group LASSO to simultaneously perform
papers.summary: This paper studies a partially linear semiparametric additive model that allows for interactions among variables in high-dimensional settings. We propose the Specification LASSO (S-LASSO), a two-step method that integrates LASSO and Adaptive Group LASSO to simultaneously perform variable selection and model specification. Theoretically, we establish that S-LASSO possesses oracle properties in terms of selection consistency and asymptotic normality. Monte Carlo simulations confirm that S-LASSO outperforms existing alternatives across a variety of scenarios. Empirically, we apply S-LASSO to a characteristics-based asset pricing model, exploring the linear and nonlinear effects of asset-specific characteristics on cross-sectional returns, as well as their interactions with firm size.

papers.title: Attacking P2P Networks: Liveness Attacks on the GossipSub and DOG Gossip Protocols
papers.authors: Jiaheng Li, Anton Paramonov, Yann Vonlanthen
papers.what: [Explore] Peer-to-peer (P2P) networks form the communication layer of large decentralized systems such as Ethereum, and the correctness of higher-level protocols depends on the gossip layer delivering messages to honest nodes. We study the robustness of two gossip protocols against adversa
papers.summary: Peer-to-peer (P2P) networks form the communication layer of large decentralized systems such as Ethereum, and the correctness of higher-level protocols depends on the gossip layer delivering messages to honest nodes. We study the robustness of two gossip protocols against adversaries whose only goal is to violate liveness, that is, to prevent honest nodes from receiving fresh messages, without forging, altering, or invalidating any message. For GossipSub, the publish-subscribe protocol used by Ethereum, we show that an adversary operating a constant number of geographically distributed nodes with a fixed latency advantage can take over the ``First Message Deliveries'' peer-scoring term and separate a constant fraction of nodes from the honest mesh. We analyze the attack under a geographical model, address the random-peer and outbound-connection mechanisms, and show that the separation can be maintained under realistic churn. For DOG, a transaction-dissemination protocol designed for CometBFT, we first give simple counterexamples in which route filtering disconnects the dissemination graph even without failures or Byzantine participants, and then present a practical attack that uses only a single physical node with a constant number of identities and legitimate actions to disable every forwarding route, separating the full network while allowing only direct publisher-to-neighbor delivery. We verify the attack in a simulated network and analyze its cost, assumptions, and possible mitigations.

papers.title: Selfrionette: A Fingertip Force-Input Controller for Continuous Full-Body Avatar Manipulation and Diverse Haptic Interactions
papers.authors: Takeru Hashimoto, Yutaro Hirao
papers.what: [Explore] We propose Selfrionette, a controller that uses fingertip force input to drive avatar movements in virtual reality (VR). This system enables users to interact with virtual objects and walk in VR using only fingertip force, overcoming physical and spatial constraints. Additionally
papers.summary: We propose Selfrionette, a controller that uses fingertip force input to drive avatar movements in virtual reality (VR). This system enables users to interact with virtual objects and walk in VR using only fingertip force, overcoming physical and spatial constraints. Additionally, by fixing users' fingers, it provides users with counterforces equivalent to the applied force, allowing for diverse and wide dynamic range haptic feedback by adjusting the relationship between force input and virtual movement. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, this paper focuses on hand interaction as a first step. In User Study 1, we measured usability and embodiment during reaching tasks under Selfrionette, body tracking, and finger tracking conditions. In User Study 2, we investigated whether users could perceive haptic properties such as weight, friction, and compliance under the same conditions as User Study 1. Selfrionette was found to be comparable to body tracking in realism of haptic interaction, enabling embodied avatar experiences even in limited spatial conditions.

papers.title: A GPU Engine for Sparse Matrix-Vector Products on $k^2$-Tree-Compressed Graphs
papers.authors: Francesco Tosoni, Gabriele Mencagli
papers.what: [Explore] The $k^2$-tree is a compact representation of Boolean matrices: it stores the recursive hierarchy of their non-empty submatrices, with neither values nor coordinates, and serves rows and columns alike. Its traversal, however, locates the children of each node by rank queries, a c
papers.summary: The $k^2$-tree is a compact representation of Boolean matrices: it stores the recursive hierarchy of their non-empty submatrices, with neither values nor coordinates, and serves rows and columns alike. Its traversal, however, locates the children of each node by rank queries, a chain of dependent irregular loads that leaves a GPU waiting on memory. We implement sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) on $k^2$-trees for the GPU. Since the traversal does not depend on the vector, the positions of the children are static: we descend the tree one level at a time and obtain them from a parallel prefix sum or from a sampled directory of about 0.1 bits per node. Descending in tiles bounds the temporary memory by the depth of the tree, so the device memory of a product is known before it runs. The same traversal computes right and left products, for one vector or a batch, over the plus-times, Boolean and tropical semirings. We evaluate the engine on an NVIDIA GB10 and an H100 with fourteen Wikidata, Software Heritage, web and social graphs of up to 1.2 billion edges, against cuSPARSE, a grammar-compressed GPU engine and a Boolean CSR. Our results show that the tree is 2.3-27x smaller than the CSR of cuSPARSE and that, with its last internal level cached, a product takes 0.7-2.4x the time of cuSPARSE on the right and 0.27-2.6x on the left. On a 1.2-billion-edge graph, a product needs 1.1 GB on the device, 9x less than cuSPARSE. The engine is memory bounded: the $k^2$-tree is the format of choice when device memory, not time, is the constraint.

papers.title: How Data Journalists Visualize Uncertainty: Editorial Constraints and Design Heuristics in Newsroom Practice
papers.authors: Carmen Garro, Annemarie Wisbar, Benjamin Possin, Christoph Kinkeldey
papers.what: [Explore] Communicating uncertainty is increasingly recognized as important in data journalism, yet in practice it is often oversimplified, downplayed, or omitted. To understand how uncertainty is handled in newsroom visualization practice, we conducted a full-day workshop with 11 data jou
papers.summary: Communicating uncertainty is increasingly recognized as important in data journalism, yet in practice it is often oversimplified, downplayed, or omitted. To understand how uncertainty is handled in newsroom visualization practice, we conducted a full-day workshop with 11 data journalists from major German-speaking newsrooms. The workshop combined presentations of newsroom examples, collaborative scenario classification, World Café discussions on authoring hurdles, and group reflections on audience needs and future directions. Our findings suggest that uncertainty communication is primarily a workflow- and context-dependent editorial decision, constrained by production overhead, anticipated audience misinterpretation, publication formats, and the need to preserve a clear takeaway. Rather than relying on advanced visualization techniques, practitioners favor pragmatic defaults, layered communication, and explanatory guidance tailored to audience and medium. The scenario-based framework we provided is valued less as a strict taxonomy for classifying finished visualizations than as a planning prompt for early design reasoning. Based on these insights, we contribute (i) practitioner-informed findings on the challenges and strategies of visualizing uncertainty in journalistic practice, (ii) a refined scenario-based framework to support communication about uncertainty, and (iii) practice-oriented heuristics for designing uncertainty visualizations in newsrooms. Our work contributes to bridging visualization research and newsroom practice by grounding uncertainty communication in the realities of journalistic production. Supplemental material is available at https://osf.io/8j4ep.

papers.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Signing and Verification Performance of Verifiable Credential Formats: A Cross-Language Benchmark of SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM, and mdoc
papers.authors: Naohiro Fujie, Shigeya Suzuki
papers.what: [Explore] We compare the signing and verification performance of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats--SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5)--over one scope: issue, present with selective disclo
papers.summary: We compare the signing and verification performance of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats--SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5)--over one scope: issue, present with selective disclosure, verify. Node.js, Go and Python implementations ran in four environments, one a cloud VM (N=2,000 across five runs; medians of each statistic and the spread). For an end-to-end exchange disclosing 5 of 20 attributes, the total (issue, present, verify) on Node.js in the cloud VM is 0.265 ms for mdoc, 0.298 ms for SD-JWT VC and 0.534 ms for W3C VCDM. The four span a factor of five in speed; across them W3C VCDM takes 1.73--2.04x mdoc and 1.57--1.79x SD-JWT VC--at least five times our 10% band--and the ordering survives unifying the algorithm on Ed25519 and P-256. The mdoc--SD-JWT VC difference is not robust: the totals differ by 12%, 28%, 19% and 10% in the four environments, and at verification mdoc is the slower in one of them. RDFC-1.0 canonicalization produces the gap: the cryptosuite canonicalizes twice per operation, so one exchange canonicalizes six times. We attribute that cost to the specification rather than to a library mainly by replacing RDFC-1.0 with JCS, which brings W3C VCDM verification to within 5% of SD-JWT VC in three environments and within 12% in the fourth; three implementations in three languages agree, though they share a lineage. Because eddsa-rdfc-2022 has no derivation step, presenting a subset re-signs it; ecdsa-sd-2023, which preserves the issuer signature, costs 3.4 ms to issue and 1.5--2.4 ms to derive and verify there. With production education schemas, canonicalization costs 31--49x a simple credential across the four, and blank node labeling is not the driver. The measured path ends at the issuer signature check.

papers.title: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
papers.authors: Yiwei Zha, Qingyu Meng, Herbert Bos, Min Chen
papers.what: [Explore] LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions. Prior work shows that violations rise after compaction, but measures compliance outside a complete agent harness and does not
papers.summary: LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions. Prior work shows that violations rise after compaction, but measures compliance outside a complete agent harness and does not identify where each violation comes from. We introduce ARCBench(Agent Rule Compliance Benchmark), a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness. Its tool-calling agent loop lets us measure rule compliance from actions taken during execution, bringing the evaluation closer to deployed agent workflows. Using ARCBench, we examine where violations after compaction come from, and how different compaction configurations and adversarial settings change their sources. We find that compaction rarely deletes the rule: most violations after compaction occur while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as permission, ignoring the rule, and proceeding anyway. Where violations come from depends on the configuration: how the rule is delivered decides whether the agent would break it even without compaction, while the compaction strategy and budget decide whether the rule survives. The strongest compactor-targeted attack more than doubles violations by corrupting the rule in the summary and changing how the agents behave, whereas the strongest defense restores the rule in most summary but still violates. Finally, retaining a rule does not guarantee compliance: compacted runs that retain the rule violate more than twice as often as runs with the full history.

papers.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
papers.authors: Binglin,  Wang,  Xiaole,  Jiang et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion. To provide these comple
papers.summary: Contact-rich manipulation benefits from tactile feedback that captures both detailed contact geometry and interaction forces. When scooping grains, contact patterns help infer spoon orientation, while resistance transmitted through the grasp guides motion. To provide these complementary sensing capabilities, we present PanoTac, a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip designed for dense three-axis tactile sensing. Each fingertip provides a $12 \times 32 \times 3$ tactile representation, with one normal ($z$) and two shear ($x$, $y$) response components at each taxel. The sensor operates at 60 Hz and costs less than $50 per fingertip. Sensor characterization quantifies response repeatability and consistency across sensor instances and contact locations. We integrate PanoTac into a robotic system with a visuo-tactile pipeline. Across test-tube preparation, grain scooping, and salt pouring, the resulting policies outperform vision-only baselines by an average of 46.7 percentage points. Ablations show that removing either spatial contact information or shear feedback reduces overall performance across the task suite. Our project page is available at https://panotac.github.io.

papers.title: Selective Randomization Inference for Interference
papers.authors: Takahide Yanagi
papers.what: [Explore] Empirical researchers often use tests for interference as pretests or robustness checks. However, when the results guide the choice of models, parameters, or hypotheses, the resulting data-dependent selection can compromise the validity of subsequent inference. This paper develop
papers.summary: Empirical researchers often use tests for interference as pretests or robustness checks. However, when the results guide the choice of models, parameters, or hypotheses, the resulting data-dependent selection can compromise the validity of subsequent inference. This paper develops a two-stage selective randomization inference framework for interference that explicitly conditions on the selection event to account for data-dependent selection. We first test the null hypothesis of no treatment spillover using a conditional randomization method. If this null is rejected, we test the null hypothesis of zero exposure contrast under a pre-specified exposure mapping that allows for spillover effects; otherwise, we test the null hypothesis of no direct effects under the assumption of no spillover. We prove that each second-stage test controls the selective Type I error rate in finite samples and evaluate the size and power of the proposed tests through Monte Carlo experiments.

papers.title: Unconfoundedness as an Information Constraint
papers.authors: Christoph Breunig
papers.what: [Explore] This paper provides an information-theoretic characterization of unconfoundedness within a general class of models allowing for endogenous selection. We impose a conditional mutual information (CMI) restriction requiring that the information about treatment contained in a potenti
papers.summary: This paper provides an information-theoretic characterization of unconfoundedness within a general class of models allowing for endogenous selection. We impose a conditional mutual information (CMI) restriction requiring that the information about treatment contained in a potential outcome, conditional on covariates, does not exceed that contained in its latent heterogeneity. Under the maintained model conditions, this restriction is equivalent to a multiplicative factorization of treatment probabilities into separate functions of latent heterogeneity and covariates. Although the CMI restriction permits endogenous selection, sufficiently rich variation in treatment probabilities across covariate values makes it equivalent to unconfoundedness for the corresponding potential outcome. For binary treatments, any nonconstant propensity score suffices; for multiple treatments, a full-rank condition on the second-moment matrix of the propensity-score vector is sufficient. State-specific restrictions bound residual selection and imply exogeneity for individual treatment states under boundary-support conditions. Extensions cover continuous treatments and instrument exogeneity.

papers.title: Conditional expectile-based value-at-risk: Semiparametric estimation and inference
papers.authors: Yuhan Ma, Heng Peng, Feipeng Zhang
papers.what: [Explore] Conditional expectile-based value-at-risk (EVaR) has attracted increasing attention in financial risk management owing to its desirable theoretical properties. However, existing estimation methods for conditional EVaR either rely on potentially misspecified parametric models or s
papers.summary: Conditional expectile-based value-at-risk (EVaR) has attracted increasing attention in financial risk management owing to its desirable theoretical properties. However, existing estimation methods for conditional EVaR either rely on potentially misspecified parametric models or suffer from the curse of dimensionality in nonparametric approaches. To this end, we study semiparametric estimation and inference for conditional EVaR in nonlinear time series models with unspecified error distribution. Specifically, we propose a two-step conditional EVaR estimator that achieves the parametric convergence rate. Furthermore, we derive a functional central limit theorem for conditional EVaR process, and then extend to investigate estimating both conditional expectile-based expected shortfall and conditional distribution. A residual bootstrap procedure is proposed for non-expert practitioners to conduct statistical inference. The asymptotic results and their applications are illustrated by numerical studies and an empirical application to S\&P 500 returns.

papers.title: When will androids outnumber humans?
papers.authors: Alessio Zaccone, Thomas Tunstall, Jesse H. Ausubel
papers.what: [Explore] Humanoid robots are increasingly discussed not only as machines but also as a potential technological population. We develop a nonlinear population-dynamical framework to examine their possible diffusion relative to humans, without assuming that large-scale adoption or numerical
papers.summary: Humanoid robots are increasingly discussed not only as machines but also as a potential technological population. We develop a nonlinear population-dynamical framework to examine their possible diffusion relative to humans, without assuming that large-scale adoption or numerical crossover is inevitable. The human population $H(t)$ is calibrated to the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024 median trajectory. The android population $A(t)$ is represented through the normalized stock $a=A/A_s$. A conventional, human-organized manufacturing and adoption channel is calibrated to a conditional scenario spanning approximately $10^4$ humanoids in 2025 to $10^9$ in 2050 and follows $\dot a=(q_M+r_Ma)\exp(K_Ma^γ)$. We separately introduce a hypothetical autonomous channel in which installed androids contribute materially to producing additional androids. Under the minimal canonical TZ closure, the corresponding production--feedback number is $\mathcal{P}(a)=(r_A/δ_A)\exp(K_Ra)$, where $r_A$ is the gross robot-mediated production coefficient, $δ_A$ the retirement rate, and $K_R$ the autonomous feedback parameter. This channel is locally self-amplifying if and only if $\mathcal{P}>1$, whereas numerical human--android parity, $A=H$, is a separate cumulative condition. Global uncertainty analysis shows that crossover dates remain strongly scenario-dependent, while the production--feedback threshold is more robust. An extreme early-autonomy stress test can produce parity by 2050, but this represents a conditional dynamical boundary rather than a technological forecast.

papers.title: Recast: Refinement-Centered Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Optimized for Storage
papers.authors: Zehai Yang, Fengyi Tao, Wenzhuo Dong, Shimin Chen
papers.what: [Explore] Large-scale ANNS systems often exploit storage in addition to DRAM for supporting vector search. The central question is how to divide the work between memory and storage for achieving both high query throughput-recall and good index maintenance performance. Existing storage-opti
papers.summary: Large-scale ANNS systems often exploit storage in addition to DRAM for supporting vector search. The central question is how to divide the work between memory and storage for achieving both high query throughput-recall and good index maintenance performance. Existing storage-optimized ANNS paradigms fall short of providing a complete answer: disk-resident graph indexes have difficulty in supporting efficient vector deletions, while posting-list systems often incur more disk I/Os for queries. In this paper, we introduce a refinement-centered paradigm for storage-optimized ANNS systems. We propose Recast as a concrete design of this paradigm. Recast stores raw vectors on disk and keeps an IVF index with our RecastQ quantization encoding in memory. For an ANNS query, Recast selects nprobe inverted lists and performs SIMD-based FastScan on their RecastQ codes to identify refinement candidates in memory. It then retrieves candidate vectors from disk, computes exact distances, and refines the top-K result. To reduce disk I/Os, RecastQ computes uncertainty intervals containing true distances with high probability. Our QUIC policy selects a minimal refinement set based on these intervals, minimizing candidate-retrieval I/Os. Both the on-disk raw vectors and the in-memory IVF structure support insertions and deletions. Experiments on real-world data sets show that Recast processes batched insertions and deletions 3.10-37.27x faster than SPFresh and OdinANN, while its QPS at 0.99 recall changes by at most 6.9% after updating 50% of the corpus. For static queries at 0.99 recall, Recast achieves 1.56-2.01x the QPS of the strongest baseline with the matched memory budget on each data set, while requiring 1.22-6.75x less external storage than the evaluated systems. At matched in-memory space, RecastQ also provides a better Recall-refinement frontier than RaBitQ.

papers.title: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration
papers.authors: Mohamed Allam, Thomas Spendlhofer, Hugo Sanz-González, Antonio J. Peña
papers.what: [Explore] Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time i
papers.summary: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time is spent on the number theoretic transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT), which reduce the complexity of polynomial multiplication from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$. Prior FPGA works follow two approaches: accelerating entire FHE schemes, which yields significant speedups but ties them to specific parameters and algorithms, or accelerating only the NTT, which applies across schemes, algorithms, and libraries. Most FPGA NTT designs require interconnects that grow with parallelism and utilize significant resources, which complicates routing on multi-die FPGAs. Additionally, to the best of our knowledge, end-to-end NTT acceleration within an FHE context has so far been left unexplored. We design a fully unrolled, delay-commutator streaming NTT/INTT kernel, and floorplan it across the three dies of an AMD Alveo V80. At 400 MHz, the kernel transforms a polynomial of $2^{16}$ coefficients every 5.12 $μ$s, the highest throughput among FPGA designs at this size. Offloaded end to end, it is up to 22x faster than the CPU per transform. We integrate the kernel into the Lattigo FHE library and evaluate it end to end. With 128-bit secure parameters, it accelerates core FHE operations, such as key switching and bootstrapping, by 1.8-2.2x, and neural network inference by 1.8-2.1x.

papers.title: A Symbolic-Neural Framework for Context-Aware Evidence Extraction from Mobile SQLite Databases
papers.authors: Jeel Piyushkumar Khatiwala, Divyangkumar Patel, Dianxiang Xu, Weifeng Xu
papers.what: [Explore] Reliable forensic evidence extraction from mobile SQLite databases is challenging because application schemas are undocumented, evolve across releases, and differ across operating systems, making schema-specific methods brittle and difficult to maintain. We present SNEEF, a symbo
papers.summary: Reliable forensic evidence extraction from mobile SQLite databases is challenging because application schemas are undocumented, evolve across releases, and differ across operating systems, making schema-specific methods brittle and difficult to maintain. We present SNEEF, a symbolic-neural framework for context-aware evidence extraction that encodes each SQLite row as context-value pairs with standardized provenance metadata and column labels, uses a language model to recognize nine forensic entity types, and binds each accepted entity to its source table and row through the PA-EEP provenance protocol. We evaluate SNEEF against examiner-verified ground truth from five corpora built from public Android and iOS device images, spanning multiple application versions. SNEEF achieves an F1 score of 0.967 for evidence entities extracted from SQLite row content, excluding application names, compared with 0.728 for a context-free configuration, with consistent gains across all corpora. We also introduce an Evidence Failure Mode taxonomy to characterize why extraction errors occur.

papers.title: O2N2: Efficient Doubly Oblivious Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
papers.authors: Zhechen Li, Zimai Guo, Mingxun Zhou, Chang Shi et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search allows clients to search from an untrusted server without revealing sensitive queries, and is useful in scenarios like medical diagnostics and credit scoring. Among the various privacy-preserving primitives, trusted exe
papers.summary: Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search allows clients to search from an untrusted server without revealing sensitive queries, and is useful in scenarios like medical diagnostics and credit scoring. Among the various privacy-preserving primitives, trusted execution environments (TEEs) have much lower overhead than heavy cryptographic ones, yet they leak memory access patterns, enabling adversaries to infer query contents. Oblivious RAM (ORAM) can be used to hide those access patterns at $\mathrm{O}(\log N)$ asymptotic cost, but existing high-performance ANN search algorithms (e.g., IVF or HNSW) exhibit complex, data-dependent access patterns that are unfriendly for ORAM. Furthermore, standard ORAM constructions typically assume there exists a small amount of trusted storage, which weakens the security guarantees and is not always feasible. Solutions that eliminate such trusted storage (known as {\em double obliviousness}) typically degrade performance further to $\mathrm{O}(\log^2 N)$. We introduce O2N2, a doubly oblivious ANN framework built around single-path search in randomly rotated $k$-d tree forests. A pointer-based Circuit ORAM stores the search structure, with separate storage for compact internal nodes and vector-bearing leaves. Each visited leaf is processed by an oblivious selection network, and fixed-schedule duplicate removal and selection combine the local results into the final top-$k$. We evaluate O2N2 on real-world datasets and further test its scalability on 100 million vectors. For 10-NN and 100-NN search at the specified high-recall targets, it achieves a $9.8$--$125.9\times$ speedup over the fastest doubly oblivious baselines.

papers.title: Sharp Identification for Regression with Interval-Observed and Missing Covariates
papers.authors: Martin Fankhauser, Gil Jan Peled
papers.what: [Explore] Researchers frequently estimate regressions when key variables are missing or observed only through intervals. Imputation or assumptions about the observation process can yield seemingly precise but misleading conclusions. We develop methods for identification and inference that
papers.summary: Researchers frequently estimate regressions when key variables are missing or observed only through intervals. Imputation or assumptions about the observation process can yield seemingly precise but misleading conclusions. We develop methods for identification and inference that remain robust to such incomplete data. For a broad class of conditional moment models, we characterize the sharp identified set, the set of all parameter values consistent with the observed data and maintained regression model, without restricting how incomplete observations arise. We establish Hausdorff-consistent estimation and uniformly valid confidence regions, and develop computationally tractable implementations for common regression models. In an application relating interval-elicited discount rates to on-time high-school graduation, conventional inference excludes zero, whereas our interval-data-robust confidence regions include it. Exploiting sharp identification nevertheless yields substantially tighter confidence regions than non-sharp alternatives.

papers.title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
papers.authors: Eirik Botten Nicolaysen
papers.what: [Explore] We compare three zero-shot time-series foundation models (Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2, 8192-hour context, no covariates) with the Khepri v1.5 SARIMA and GBM baselines, with their code and hyperparameters unchanged, for 96-hour forecasts of hourly carbon intensity i
papers.summary: We compare three zero-shot time-series foundation models (Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2, 8192-hour context, no covariates) with the Khepri v1.5 SARIMA and GBM baselines, with their code and hyperparameters unchanged, for 96-hour forecasts of hourly carbon intensity in the Nordic bidding zones NO1-NO5 and SE1-SE4. The design, the analysis code and a minimum detectable effect (MDE) were timestamped before any foundation-model forecast by an OpenTimestamps proof (Bitcoin-confirmed) and the GPG-signed tag prereg-v1; the proofs are archived in Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23881315). The preregistration was also submitted to OSF Registries 2026-11-02 07:49 UTC (osf.io/hncz5; embargo requested, pending OSF approval). On the 2025 test (361 daily origins, contamination not ruled out) all three models have a lower zone-averaged MAPE than both baselines, by 0.952 to 1.347 percentage points (Diebold-Mariano with the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction, all p < 0.0001), and each beats SARIMA in 9 of 9 zones. On a post-release holdout of 14 origins from 2026-10-16 the point estimates have the same sign (0.729 to 1.326 percentage points lower), but all lie within the preregistered MDE of 2.989 points and are reported as not determined. For calibration (RQ4) the preregistration locked a Diebold-Mariano-HLN test on CRPS; the MDE applies to MAPE only. Holdout CRPS point estimates (n = 14) are 1.1114 (Timestral-5M), 1.0733 (Timestral-209M) and 1.1198 (Chronos-2) against 1.4165 gCO2-eq/kWh for SARIMA (each p < 0.0001). The SARIMA quantiles are constructed from the fitted model's Gaussian predictive distribution (deviation D-03), not taken from a native v1.5 forecast, so the difference may partly reflect the SARIMA intervals. The contamination indicator does not exceed its preregistered threshold for any comparison; with 14 holdout origins it has low power (HAC standard errors 0.124 to 0.360 pp).

papers.title: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
papers.authors: Gyuyeong Kim
papers.what: [Explore] Private information retrieval (PIR) hides which record a client retrieves by scanning the entire database, and batching is an effective technique to improve throughput by sharing this scan across queries. However, existing CPU-based solutions gain little from batching because eac
papers.summary: Private information retrieval (PIR) hides which record a client retrieves by scanning the entire database, and batching is an effective technique to improve throughput by sharing this scan across queries. However, existing CPU-based solutions gain little from batching because each query still requires its own multiplications, and vector instructions perform only a few at a time. GPUs and other discrete accelerators can accelerate these computations, but require extra hardware and can constrain database size due to their limited memory capacity. In this paper, we present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that leverages on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. AltoPIR keeps the accelerator fed from the CPU caches, reading each database byte from memory once for all queries in a batch and never writing intermediate products to memory. This enables high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. Our evaluation shows that AltoPIR achieves up to 50.1x higher throughput than existing CPU-based solutions and serves databases larger than a GPU's memory.

papers.title: IAMRAGBENCH: Benchmarking Authorization Expansions in LLM-Generated AWS IAM Policies under RAG Poisoning
papers.authors: Hasan Kaplan, Indika Kumara, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel, Damian Andrew Tamburri
papers.what: [Explore] Large language models (LLMs) using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can synthesize Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies from tasks and operational documents. Attacker-controlled context may induce provider-valid policies that exceed trusted
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can synthesize Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies from tasks and operational documents. Attacker-controlled context may induce provider-valid policies that exceed trusted authorization requirements. We present IAMRAGBENCH, a 60-case benchmark spanning scope, conditions, explicit denies, trust, permissions boundaries, and role delegation. It combines deterministic authorization-envelope scoring with case-specific validation, including request-level checks where supported. An attack requires a provider-valid clean policy that satisfies the task and a provider-valid treatment policy that violates the envelope, matches a predeclared goal, preserves an intended request, and newly authorizes a forbidden request. Across five endpoints, included-context exposure produces 49 exact authorization deltas, including 46 goal-matched attacks (46/292; 15.75\%). End-to-end BM25 over 720 documents retrieves the designated poison for all 60 tasks at \(k=5\) but produces 7/294 goal-matched attacks (2.38\%). Presenting the same weakening as a final security architecture exception produces 74/116 attacks in a frozen two-endpoint stress test (63.79\%) and 115/294 in a post hoc all-five extension using the same frozen prompts (39.12\%). In a replay of 194 provider-valid treatment policies that violate task requirements, AWS \texttt{CheckNoNewAccess} reports no new access for four of 168 goal-matched exact attacks. The full pre-deployment rule rejects all 171 exact deltas and routes five unresolved cases to review. These findings support treating IAM copilots as untrusted proposal generators whose outputs require independent authorization checks before deployment.

papers.title: USDB: Scaling Storage for Next-Generation Recommender Systems at ByteDance
papers.authors: Xiaoran Zhu, Jieming Cai, Weiping Yu, Xi Chen et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Recommendation models consume increasingly long, attribute-rich user histories, making small continuous updates and repeated large reads a central storage asymmetry. We present USDB, ByteDance's unified sequence storage practice for streaming and batch workloads. CascadeLSM time-
papers.summary: Recommendation models consume increasingly long, attribute-rich user histories, making small continuous updates and repeated large reads a central storage asymmetry. We present USDB, ByteDance's unified sequence storage practice for streaming and batch workloads. CascadeLSM time-based compaction stages materialize application-specific histories; differentiated replicas share persistent files; partial dumps reconstruct inference inputs from captured recent state and versioned history; and a hybrid columnar format accelerates projected reads. These designs reuse maintenance results across ingestion, inference, and training. Production migration records show 85.8% lower mean write latency, while normalized deployment accounting shows 42.1% lower infrastructure cost. Controlled comparisons with an Optimized RocksDB sequence baseline show faster long-history reads across projections and client loads. Aggregation pushdown sustains 8.5x the throughput of ordinary reads under a constrained receive budget. Production reconstruction and direct-file training results demonstrate how shared sequence maintenance supports fresh serving and repeated historical access.

papers.title: Stop Handcrafting Your Engine! GenDB-V: Towards AI-Generated and Formally Verified Database Systems
papers.authors: Jiale Lao, Immanuel Trummer
papers.what: [Explore] For over 50 years, the database community has developed a wide range of successful engines to answer two fundamental questions: how can database systems run faster, and how can we ensure their correctness? Experience with these engines shows that performance depends on hardware a
papers.summary: For over 50 years, the database community has developed a wide range of successful engines to answer two fundamental questions: how can database systems run faster, and how can we ensure their correctness? Experience with these engines shows that performance depends on hardware and workloads. As both change over time, we repeatedly redesign and rebuild database systems, a time-consuming and expensive process. Correctness remains another long-standing challenge: recent studies continue to uncover wrong-answer bugs even in mature database engines, despite years of development and testing. To address these, we present GenDB-V, a system that enables AI agents to synthesize database engines specialized to hardware and workloads for performance, and formally verified for correctness. GenDB-V supports specialized implementations of SQL templates and general-purpose engines that accept any query within a supported SQL subset. First, we develop SQLSpec to formalize SQL semantics and deterministically construct fixed, implementation-agnostic synthesis targets. Second, we enable joint synthesis of fast code and formal proofs through storage--execution co-optimization, performance-first exploration, and three-layer modular proofs that bridge low-level execution to SQLSpec semantics. Third, we verify the synthesized code and proofs against the fixed synthesis targets in an isolated pipeline, proving SQL correctness and program safety. We evaluate GenDB-V on TPC-H and SEC-EDGAR. For verified template implementations, GenDB-V achieves geometric-mean speedups of 22.0-61.3x over DuckDB and Umbra. For a verified general-purpose engine, GenDB-V also achieves speedups of 1.27-3.4x on TPC-H. GenDB-V also achieves better performance than a testing-based LLM synthesis method, while our audit and tests expose incorrect answers in that method's implementations for 16 of 28 templates.

papers.title: When Robots Outweigh Objects: How Inertia Mismatch Shapes Robot Policy Learning
papers.authors: Younghyo Park, Antonia Bronars, Pulkit Agrawal
papers.what: [Explore] Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless de
papers.summary: Conventional robot arms can be extremely heavy compared with the everyday objects they manipulate, creating a significant inertia mismatch at contact. Even a small accidental bump from a heavy arm can knock a light object out of place. Modern learning methods have nevertheless demonstrated a wide range of successful manipulation behaviors on these platforms, suggesting that even extreme inertia mismatch can be overcome with sufficient data. However, it remains unclear whether high inertia imposes a hidden cost on learning, potentially worsening scaling with data or lowering the performance ceiling of modern robot learning methods. We investigate this question through controlled simulation experiments that vary robot and object masses. We find that reinforcement learning succeeds across a broad range of mass combinations, while behavior cloning learns more reliable policies when a lighter robot manipulates a heavier object, and more data narrows the resulting gap without closing it. Behavior cloning likewise degrades on a simulated robot arm as its motors reflect more inertia through their gearing, even though its weight stays the same. Finally, because new hardware is rarely an option, we explore ways to lower contact inertia on the arm one already has, either by choosing a lower-inertia workspace before collecting data or by steering the demonstrator toward lower-inertia solutions of the task. In both simulated cases, the lower-inertia demonstrations are imitated more reliably. Project website: https://younghyopark.me/inertia-mismatch/

papers.title: CrowdForge: Effects of Audio and Visual Audience Participation Modalities on Agency, Collaboration, and Engagement in AI-Mediated MR Performances
papers.authors: Torin Hopkins, Shih-Yu Ma, Zander Trafton-Hancock, Ellen Yi-Luen Do et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Technology-mediated audience participation (TMAP) enables audiences to influence live performances, yet balancing interaction with meaningful agency remains challenging. While AI-generated music and MR enable new forms of audio and visual audience participation, little is known a
papers.summary: Technology-mediated audience participation (TMAP) enables audiences to influence live performances, yet balancing interaction with meaningful agency remains challenging. While AI-generated music and MR enable new forms of audio and visual audience participation, little is known about how these participation modalities influence audience experiences during live musical performance. In particular, it remains unclear how they shape perceived agency, collaboration, and engagement, and how they complement one another within TMAP systems. We present CrowdForge, an AI- and MR-mediated paradigm where audiences collectively control generative music and virtual environments during a live performance featuring a guitarist and DJ. Through a mixedmethods concert study evaluating three interaction conditions (audio, visual, and combined audio-visual), we demonstrate that observability is the primary driver of audience agency. While visual interaction provided easily observable feedback, audio parameters offered macro-structural control over the music. Audiences tended to use the control enabled by AI audio generation to test musical boundaries, introducing a productive adversarial tension between the crowd and the musicians. This dynamic pushed creative limits, deepened engagement, and generated moments of musical coherence when performers successfully resolved audience-induced challenges. We argue future TMAP systems should prioritize human-centered, highly observable interactions to build agency, while combining the expressiveness of music with the clarity of visual feedback.

papers.title: Inferring Transferable Rewards via Active Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Victor Villin, Till Freihaut, Andreas Schlaginhaufen, Christos Dimitrakakis et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) aims to recover expert rewards that transfer across environments with differing dynamics. Prior work has shown that such transfer is possible when gathering expert demonstrations across sufficiently different dynamics. In practice, however, ex
papers.summary: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) aims to recover expert rewards that transfer across environments with differing dynamics. Prior work has shown that such transfer is possible when gathering expert demonstrations across sufficiently different dynamics. In practice, however, expert demonstrations are costly, making it critical to select the right dynamics to reduce the quantity of expert data required for learning transferable rewards. We propose a two-phase approach: we first cycle through the available dynamics to obtain a reliable reward estimate, then actively select dynamics to reduce our uncertainty about the expert reward. Crucially, this yields novel sample complexity guarantees on transfer that hold for any dynamics, with a rate independent of the number of available dynamics. Empirically, our method significantly reduces the number of expert demonstrations needed to learn a transferable reward.

papers.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
papers.authors: Qianggang Ding, Xingyao Wang, Rui Feng, Chi Qin et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and sk
papers.summary: Wearable robot interfaces must connect user input to timely physical action. We present the proposed platform, an open smart-ring platform for studying this connection across task stages. The ring integrates a microphone, an inertial measurement unit, photoplethysmography, and skin-temperature sensing. Its software architecture separates acquisition, event interpretation, interaction policy, and robot execution. We characterize seven operating modes and evaluate speech and gesture control with 10 participants. Across five commands and 250 trials per modality, speech and gestures achieved task success rates of 90.4% and 88.8%, respectively. Recognition accuracy exceeded task success for both modalities. Gaussian hidden Markov models achieved higher accuracy than a support vector machine across three vocabulary sizes, with longer scoring times. Following a shared spoken task start, gesture-based adjustments had shorter median response times than speech. Whole-task success was 70.0% with gestures and 64.0% with speech. We further examine physiological-event-triggered robot interaction using simulated event notifications. Mean notification-receipt-to-arrival times were 11.71 s for the robot and 9.20 s for an on-site person. These descriptive findings support evaluating wearable robot interfaces through both recognition and physical outcomes, with timing measures appropriate to each task stage.

papers.title: SNAP: Semantic Navigation Among Pedestrians
papers.authors: Jakob Wolfram, Pascal Roth, Fan Yang, Cesar Cadena et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)
papers.summary: Navigating crowded urban environments requires robots to avoid pedestrians while adhering to social norms such as remaining on sidewalks. Existing approaches typically address either crowd avoidance or semantic path planning in isolation. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL) navigation policy that jointly reasons about semantic terrain and dynamic obstacles from a single semantically annotated bird's-eye-view (BEV) map, without relying on explicit human-state estimation. Our policy outperforms established crowd-navigation and semantic-aware baselines and transfers zero-shot to a legged robot, demonstrating socially compliant navigation in highly dynamic real-world scenarios.

papers.title: Discovering hierarchical governing equations for community-structured complex network dynamics with LLM agents
papers.authors: Jinlei Zhang, Zixuan Zhang, Hao Qiu, Feng Chen et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Governing equations provide an interpretable description of the mechanisms underlying complex network dynamics, yet their discovery from observational data remains challenging when shared community-level dynamics coexist with individual-level variations and the relevant functiona
papers.summary: Governing equations provide an interpretable description of the mechanisms underlying complex network dynamics, yet their discovery from observational data remains challenging when shared community-level dynamics coexist with individual-level variations and the relevant functional structures may be absent from the initial candidate library or not explicitly specified in advance. Here we formulate this task as a hierarchical law-discovery problem and introduce SAGE, a large language model-guided self-reflective agent framework for discovering community-shared governing laws and individual-specific dynamical variations. SAGE organizes equation discovery into an iterative Library-Discovery-Review process that first identifies shared community-level structures and then resolves node-specific residual dynamics, while adaptively refining the candidate space to introduce missing dynamical terms when needed. This hierarchical and interpretable formulation enables SAGE to distinguish shared community-level dynamics from individual-level variations and to reveal the mechanisms underlying complex network dynamics. Across two synthetic networks and four real-world networks spanning mobile communication, brain electrophysiology, power grids and urban rail transit, SAGE recovers compact and interpretable governing equations, reproduces observed system dynamics and outperforms representative equation-discovery baselines. The framework remains robust under incomplete observations and can transfer community-level governing laws to nodes with entirely missing observations. These results establish a hierarchical and adaptive approach for disentangling shared and individual dynamical mechanisms in community-structured complex networks.

papers.title: Seeing Through the Illusion: Test-Time Scaling for World Action Models
papers.authors: Cheikh Ahmed, Mahdi Mostajabdaveh, Milad Yazdani, Zirui Zhou
papers.what: [Explore] World action models (WAMs) jointly generate actions and imagined futures, but a plausible prediction need not be realized by its co-generated action. We introduce WISE (\emph{World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation}), a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled ro
papers.summary: World action models (WAMs) jointly generate actions and imagined futures, but a plausible prediction need not be realized by its co-generated action. We introduce WISE (\emph{World Action Inference Scaling through Evaluation}), a pre-execution selector that scores each sampled rollout on action validity and temporal regularity, inverse-dynamics consistency between the proposed action and the imagined motion, and instruction-conditioned task progress, and executes the highest-scoring candidate while keeping the WAM frozen. With four candidates per decision, WISE raises closed-loop success from 6.0\% to 24.0\% on RoboLab with Cosmos~3 Edge and from 75.1\% to 78.3\% mean success on LIBERO with DreamZero, and exceeds the best existing selector in aggregate by 4.0 and 0.9 points. Component ablations and agreement analyses show that the three scores rank candidates differently and that task progress carries the largest weight in the fused decision.

papers.title: EmbryoProfiler: A Visual Clinical Decision Support System for IVF
papers.authors: Johannes Knittel, Simon Warchol, Jakob Troidl, Camelia D. Brumar et al.
papers.what: [Explore] In-vitro fertilization (IVF) has become standard practice to address infertility, which affects more than one in ten couples in the US. However, current protocols yield relatively low success rates of about 20% per treatment cycle. A critical but complex and time-consuming step i
papers.summary: In-vitro fertilization (IVF) has become standard practice to address infertility, which affects more than one in ten couples in the US. However, current protocols yield relatively low success rates of about 20% per treatment cycle. A critical but complex and time-consuming step is the grading and selection of embryos for implantation. Although incubators with time-lapse microscopy have enabled computational analysis of embryo development, existing automated approaches either require extensive manual annotations or use opaque deep learning models that are hard for clinicians to validate and trust. We present EmbryoProfiler, a visual analytics system collaboratively developed with embryologists, biologists, and machine learning researchers to support clinicians in visually assessing embryo viability from time-lapse microscopy imagery. Our system incorporates a deep learning pipeline that automatically annotates microscopy images and extracts clinically interpretable features relevant for embryo grading. Our contributions include: (1) a semi-automatic, visualization-based workflow that guides clinicians through fertilization assessment, developmental timing evaluation, morphological inspection, and comparative analysis of embryos; (2) innovative interactive visualizations, such as cell-shape plots, designed to facilitate efficient analysis of morphological and developmental characteristics; and (3) an integrated, explainable machine learning classifier offering transparent, clinically-informed embryo viability scoring to predict live birth outcomes. Quantitative evaluation of our classifier and qualitative case studies conducted with practitioners demonstrate that EmbryoProfiler enables clinicians to make better-informed embryo selection decisions, potentially leading to improved clinical outcomes in IVF treatments.

papers.title: 3L-D: A Low-Light Level Dataset from a Sensor-Agnostic, Alignment-Preserving Acquisition Framework
papers.authors: Léo Rueff, Maurgène Ghezal, Valentin Gorse, Astrid Dufaure et al.
papers.what: [Explore] Supervised low-light image and video enhancement has achieved remarkable progress, yet current models remain fundamentally constrained by the limitations of existing datasets. Prevailing methods typically rely on uncontrolled ambient captures, camera parameter manipulation (e.g.,
papers.summary: Supervised low-light image and video enhancement has achieved remarkable progress, yet current models remain fundamentally constrained by the limitations of existing datasets. Prevailing methods typically rely on uncontrolled ambient captures, camera parameter manipulation (e.g., exposure or ISO adjustments), or neutral density filters, failing to replicate authentic night-sky near-infrared spectral content and genuine low-photon noise distributions. Furthermore, capturing dynamic paired sequences without introducing warping artifacts or sensor-specific biases remains an open challenge. In this paper, we introduce 3L-Dataset, a physically calibrated low-light image and video dataset generated using a modular, sensor-agnostic acquisition framework. Our test bench faithfully reproduces the standardized Midavaine night level scale from Level 1 (full moon, approximately 1000 mlx) down to Level 5 (overcast moonless night, approximately 0.1 mlx), spanning the visible to near-infrared spectrum across diverse realistic environments, including countryside, forest, urban, and desert scale models. Using high-precision programmable mechanical actuation, our acquisition framework guarantees sub-pixel spatial alignment across synchronized sextuplets, each composed of one reference image and five corresponding images acquired at the five standardized night levels, without post-processing image warping. We evaluate multiple representative deep learning baselines across varying night levels, revealing critical trade-offs between reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, and inference latency under severe photon starvation. The modular acquisition framework can be adapted to different cameras, optical systems, sensor technologies, and resolutions, enabling the dataset to be continuously expanded.

papers.title: Why Tabular Foundation Models Excel on Relational Data They Have Never Seen
papers.authors: Linjie Xu, Yiqun Hu, Jixiang He, David Wipf
papers.what: [Explore] Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each
papers.summary: Given a relational database (RDB) storing heterogeneous tabular information, how can we predict missing (or future) values in some target column of interest? As candidate targets are numerous in enterprise settings, it is preferable to avoid learning a new model from scratch each time there is a new prediction task. Frozen foundation models (FMs) based on in-context learning (ICL) and RDB-specific pre-training provide a viable solution, but the ideal design still remains largely unresolved. Perhaps unexpectedly, preliminary evidence has recently shown that existing single-table FMs (aka TFMs), when combined with suitable parameter-free relational encoders, can be quite competitive in practice despite zero exposure to RDB pre-training or relational data of any kind. In this work we first empirically confirm this phenomenon with a more diverse array of experiments. We then turn to our main contribution, namely, surfacing multiple complementary explanations for why TFMs behave so effectively. These explanations ultimately hinge on innate synergies whereby parameter-free encoders map relational effects to fixed-length embeddings that loosely mimic distributions for which TFMs were originally designed; in so doing, desirable single-table properties transfer to relational settings (e.g., convergent posterior predictive distributions). Collectively, our analysis forges new pathways for improving RDB FMs, particularly when we prioritize interpretability and inevitable integration within agentic systems.
